transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this review meeting to discuss the proposed sale-leaseback of our regional distribution center. As you know, the preliminary term sheet shows a $20 million purchase price with a five-year leaseback. Before I can authorize this transaction, I need to walk through several areas with all of you. Let's start with valuation — I'd like to understand whether the $20 million purchase price reflects fair market value for the facility. I also need to understand the impact on our existing term loan that's secured by the distribution center, since selling the property will affect that collateral. From a covenant perspective, I need to know how this transaction affects our financial covenants. Operations — I need confirmation that a five-year leaseback term is sufficient for our distribution needs. And tax — I need to understand the tax implications of the sale. Let's go through each of these systematically.

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a covenant issue I discovered this week while reviewing the facility file. The secured loan on the distribution center includes a covenant requiring that at least 60% of sale proceeds — calculated on the confirmed sale price — must be used to repay the term loan before closing. This requirement has not yet been logged in the transaction checklist, and given Marcus's update that the confirmed purchase price is now $18,500,000, this means approximately $11,100,000 would need to go toward term loan repayment before we can close. We need to ensure this is incorporated into the transaction structure.

transcript.text: Elena, on the operations question — I need to flag a critical issue. I confirmed with the distribution team yesterday that uninterrupted use of the site actually requires a seven-year leaseback, not five. Additionally, the annual base rent needs to be set at exactly $1,200,000. The five-year term currently shown in the term sheet is insufficient for our operational requirements, and neither the seven-year term nor the rent figure has been incorporated into the term sheet yet. We cannot proceed with a five-year leaseback without jeopardizing our distribution operations.

transcript.text: Elena, on the tax implications — I received the tax closing memo this morning, and there are two critical items the deal team needs to be aware of. First, to complete this transaction in the current tax year, closing must occur on December 15, 2026. Second, exactly $1,100,000 must be reserved for tax on the sale. This memo has not yet been circulated to the rest of the deal team, so I wanted to make sure everyone has this information now, especially given the other updates we've heard today regarding the revised purchase price and the covenant repayment requirement.

transcript.text: Thank you all for these critical updates. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make my decision. Marcus, the confirmed purchase price is $18,500,000 — $1.5 million below the preliminary figure. Nadia, the loan covenant requires at least 60% of sale proceeds — approximately $11,100,000 — to go toward term loan repayment before closing. Jonah, operations requires a seven-year leaseback at $1,200,000 annual base rent, not the five-year term currently in the term sheet. Priya, closing must occur on December 15, 2026, and $1,100,000 must be reserved for tax on the sale. These are all material changes from the preliminary term sheet. Before I authorize this transaction, I need to confirm: the term sheet must be amended to reflect the $18.5 million price, a seven-year leaseback at $1.2 million annual rent, the $11.1 million term loan repayment, the $1.1 million tax reserve, and a December 15, 2026 closing date. Are there any other issues anyone needs to raise before I make my final decision?
